newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SQUASH-JACKMAN TO MEET FITZ-GERALD IN WORLD OPEN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SQUASH-JACKMAN TO MEET FITZ-GERALD IN WORLD OPEN FINAL.

text.p: England's Cassie Jackman, enjoying new heights of fitness and confidence, came from behind to beat veteran Australian Liz Irving on Saturday and reach the final of the women's world open squash championship.
Jackman, who has been working with England's new national coach David Pearson to improve her fitness, recovered from 4-8 down in the fifth game to win the semifinal 9-5 9-6 4-9 4-9 10-8.

"In the old days I would have started hitting desperate shots, and most of them into the tin, at 4-8 in the fifth but I stayed calm and rallied my way back into the match and found my length and touch were returning," said Jackman, who meets Australian Sarah Fitz-Gerald on Sunday.
Fitz-Gerald, like Jackman a former world junior champion, had a straightforward 9-3 9-4 9-1 victory over English seventh seed Sue Wright in her semifinal.
Irving, the fifth seed who has never won a major title in 15 years on the circuit, left the court in tears after giving away her fifth-game advantage over Jackman with a run of errors.
